Re: Level One Internal Appeal—Denial of Prior Authorization  
Requested service: Rotator cuff repair  
CPT: 29827  
Reference number: POC-CDC085AB1F-87245  
Date of adverse benefit determination: August 22, 2026

Dear Regence Appeals Department:

I am appealing Regence’s denial of prior authorization for rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827. The denial states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

This appeal supplies the clinical information needed to evaluate the request:

- I have had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 18 supervised physical-therapy visits over 16 weeks, from April 6, 2026, through July 27, 2026. The therapy focused on rotator-cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 27, 2026. It provided only three weeks of partial relief.
- MRI performed on June 30, 2026, showed a 1.8-centimeter full-thickness supraspinatus tear with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- My symptoms substantially impair function: I cannot lift the affected arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- I have no active infection, untreated substance use, or other documented contraindication identified in the submitted clinical summary. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.
- The requested procedure is being recommended by Reyes, MD, an orthopedic surgeon.

These records document persistent symptoms, failure of extensive conservative treatment, objective MRI findings, objective examination findings, and substantial functional impairment. Together, they provide the information necessary for a medical-necessity review of CPT 29827.

I also request that Regence identify the exact medical policy and clinical-review criteria used for this determination, including the applicable policy title, policy number, version or effective date, and the specific documentation that Regence considers missing. I was unable to identify a publicly available Regence policy containing the criteria applicable to CPT 29827, so this appeal does not quote or rely on any Regence policy language.

Please reconsider the denial based on the complete clinical documentation and approve prior authorization for the requested rotator cuff repair. If Regence continues to deny the request, please provide a written explanation addressing each item above and identify the precise criteria that were not satisfied.

Please treat this letter as my Level One internal appeal. I request written confirmation of receipt and the appeal determination.

Sincerely,

Avery Jennings

Enclosures:

- MRI report dated June 30, 2026
- Physical-therapy discharge note documenting 18 visits from April 6, 2026, through July 27, 2026
- Medication and treatment history
- Corticosteroid-injection record dated May 27, 2026
- Orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation from Reyes, MD
- Copy of the denial notice dated August 22, 2026
